_note: Generated race tracks (Phase 5: track/). A track is its seed + its parameters + the generator's version: the same three always make the same track (track/generate.js). presets: what the track generator page and the Track scene offer. How each style builds its layout and the limits every track keeps to (the tightest corner, run-off, gradients, banking…) belong to a generator version and never change with it: track/gen/v1.js STYLES and LIMITS. build: the road and ground made from a track (track/build.js; not part of a track's identity). surfaces: the road, its verges and the ground round it (as Map v3's: the tyres and the effects). themes (Phase 5 Step 2, version-2 tracks): each theme's dress settings say what goes where (run-off sizes and types, the barrier, how many grandstands, trees, rocks, buildings…) and are part of a version-2 track's identity like the generator's rules (tests/fixtures/tracks-v2.json pins tracks of every theme: if they change, a theme's dress settings changed — make it a new generator version instead); look is how it looks (colours, sky, the time of day and weather), free to change. barriers: the barrier types (as Map v3's railings: thick colliders taller than drawn, overlapping at every joint). brands: the advertising (fictional, all of them). dressTests and performance: the targets the tests hold dressed tracks to.

params._note: type: circuit (a closed loop) or p2p (a sprint or hillclimb). lengthKm: [min, max]. corners: [min, max] corner groups (a chicane or esses count as one). style: flowing, technical, fast or mixed. width: m. elevation: m from the lowest point to the highest. climb (p2p): m from start to finish (negative: downhill). banking: the most banking in fast corners, degrees (0: none). crests: sharper rises and dips allowed. bridges: the track may cross itself on a bridge (not yet built: always false). Version 2 adds: theme (one of themes, or auto: chosen by the seed), pitLane (a circuit: a pit lane beside the main straight), sausages (raised kerbs at chicanes), dressing (0–63: another dressing of the same layout).

build._note: The road and the ground (track/build.js). step: m between cross-sections of the road mesh. verge: m of flat run-off either side, the same height as the road's edge, left for kerbs and barriers (Phase 5 Step 2). margin: m of ground round the track. cell: the ground grid's spacing (m, at least; bigger tracks: bigger cells, at most maxCells across). blend: m over which the ground meets the land round it. Version-2 tracks: the run-off, kerbs and barriers come from the dressing (track/dress.js); kerb: the flat kerb's width and height (m), its ridges' spacing, the sausage kerb's; runoffFall: how steeply run-off falls away from the road's edge; lip: m of verge beyond the kerbs' width before the run-off (its gravel, grass) begins.

surfaces._note: What the tyres drive on (physics/vehicle.js): grip, rollingResistance (also what a car must push past to move off: in a gravel trap more than its tyres can, so a car that stops there is beached), plough (a gravel trap's drag on a wheel ploughing through it, a share of its load: physics/vehicle.js), marks (skid marks), sound, effects (what tyres throw up), rumble (a kerb's: the sound's rattle).

barriers._note: Barrier types (track/build.js; map/build/format/barriers.js makes their colliders, as Map v3's railings): height and thickness drawn; the collider at least minThickness thick and extraHeight taller (nothing hops or slips through; the cars use continuous collision detection besides). restitution: how much a car bounces off; friction: how it slides along; material: what the damage and the crash sounds take it to be (a tyre wall's 'tyres': softer — physics/settings.json impacts.materials). armco: steel guard rail; concrete: a wall; tyres: a tyre wall (in front of a rail) at the end of fast corners' run-off; pitbox: the garages' fronts; pitwall: between the track and the pit lane.

themes._note: Environment themes (Phase 5 Step 2). dress: what goes where — runoff: scale × the speed-based size (track/dress.js), at least min and at most max m beyond the road's edge; fast / medium / slow: the run-off types of corners taken that fast (weights), straight: beside the straights; barrier: the usual barrier (concrete wherever the run-off is under 4 m; tyre walls at the end of fast corners' run-off); fence: 'all' (catch fencing everywhere) or none (only by the grandstands); grandstands; marshalEvery (m); lightTowers; boards (advertising); footbridge (the chance of one); buildings (count, style: city lines the track, others stand well away; height range); trees and rocks (count, clumps, how near and far from the barrier, kinds by weight). look: colours (ground, run-off, verge, buildings…), sky, fog, sun (the time of day) and weather (track/render.js themeEnvironment), backdrop (distant hills, mountains, the sea, a skyline).

dressTests._note: What the dressing tests hold dressed tracks to (tests/track-dress.mjs, tests/track-dress-drive.ts). runoff: a car going straight on at the racing line's speed where each corner turns in, braking hard — it stops, or hits the barrier at most maxImpactKmh or at most slowedTo of the speed it left at, on at least minShare of corners. barrier: impact speeds (km/h) and angles (°) for every barrier type. gravel: speeds driven straight into a gravel trap, the speed (km/h) below which a car coasting in must be beached (can't drive out), the least deceleration (m/s²) in it. placement: how many seeds (every preset and theme).

performance._note: Targets for dressed tracks (tests/track-dress.mjs; the browser's in the smoke test): loadSeconds — making and building a track (Node; the browser's worker about the same); cachedMs — loading one made before; drawCalls — the whole dressed world drawn (the track, its dressing, no cars); frameMs — physics for 8 cars a frame at 60 fps (Node: a race's worst sustained step).

detail._note: The track detail setting (Phase 5 Step 4: the player's, in the settings — track/renderDress.js dressMeshes detail, testtrack/test-scene.js): scenery — the share of trees and rocks drawn; treeNear — metres within which trees are drawn in full; spectators — the grandstands' crowd; shadows — whether the dressing casts them, and the sun's shadow map (0: none); pixelRatio — the most of the screen's own. Its targets (tests/track-perf.ts, the browser's track perf check): loadSeconds — each of 50 tracks in a row made, built and drawn; memoryGrowthMb — the heap from the 10th load to the 50th; cpuFrameMs — the CPU's share of a frame in an 8-car race on the busiest theme (physics, the dressing's updates, the replay's recording: tests/track-perf.ts); frameMs — the whole frame there, the 95th percentile, in a browser (tools/track-perf-browser.mjs); drawCalls — the dressed world.

conditions._note: Time of day and weather (Phase 5 Step 4: track/renderDress.js themeEnvironment, track/weather.js). A track event's conditions (quest conditions.timeOfDay / weather; 'any': its theme's) or the theme's own. times: each time of day's hour (effects/lighting.js lightAt) and warmth (the sky's and sun's tint toward gold); a quest's dawn / day / dusk / night: event (day: the theme's own if it's daytime). weather: sunScale (the sun's strength), grey (the sky toward grey), fogScale (the fog's distances), rain (streaks: drops a second near the camera), wet (the road darker and shinier) and grip (the tyres' grip on a wet road: used only if applyGrip — the hook for when the weather system changes grip; until then it's how it looks). floodlit: a circuit at night (or dusk) lit by floodlights — the light towers lit, masts at the marshal posts where a theme has no towers, and the lighting's own: the ambient light's colour and strength and a key light from above.

variety._note: The variety report (npm run track-variety: tools/track-variety.mjs, docs/TRACK_GENERATOR.md 'Variety report'): per tracks of every preset made and measured; similarity: sample tracks' layouts compared pair by pair, a pair more alike than duplicate is a near-duplicate. targets (all: every preset's; a preset's own over them): failed (seeds with no track, at most), gateP10 / gateP50 (the quality gate's 10th percentile and median, at least), passQuick (the share reaching the quick races' gate), allThree (the share with slow, medium and fast corners), signature (the share with a signature feature), lengthCover (p10–p90 of length against the preset's range), themeMin (a preset on auto: every theme, the rarest at least this share), duplicates (near-duplicate pairs, at most), elevationP50 (m, median).

quality._note: A generated track's quality score (Phase 5 Step 4: track/quality.js, docs/TRACK_GENERATOR.md 'Quality score'). Each part 0-1, the score their weighted mean × 100. variety: corners by apex speed (the race car's speed plan: slow under slowBelow km/h, fast from fastFrom), their mix (entropy) and how often a corner is the same as the last (radius within sameRadius, turn within sameTurn °; repeatFull: that share counts as none at all); enough corners for full marks. flow: braking zones (a drop of brakeDrop km/h or more); a heavy one (heavyDrop) after a run of under minRun m from the last is stop-start; allow (or share of the zones) of them is no flow at all. overtaking: a braking zone from at least minTop km/h, dropping minDrop, after a run of minRun m: want of them on a circuit (wantShort on one under shortTrack m), wantSprint on a sprint. elevation: crests and dips (a local high or low over ± window m, prominence m above or below), corners with a grade of cornerGrade at the apex, the range; each's share of the part and how many make full marks. safety: the run-off outside each corner's apex against what its speed asks for (share of the speed rule, at most capMetres), weighted by speed²; a corner with an apex of fastApex km/h or more and under dangerRatio of it is a dangerous spot, as is a stretch of 20 m or more at closeKmh or faster with another part of the track within closeMetres beyond its edge; each costs dangerCost. ai: an NPC race's closeness (cars NPCs of skill in the skill range, laps laps, on their own: tests/track-events.ts 'close', the test page's Race AI) — the finishers' spread (fullSpread of the winner's time: none at all) and overtakes (passesPerCar each: full marks); bunched: its share; maxSpread: the median spread the close-races test allows (a guard: a broken start or a blocked track spreads the field far wider). weights: each part's. min: the gate score (the deterministic parts) the day's, week's and quick tracks must reach (track/events/model.js).
